response.sql:
WITH per_id_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(ANA) as avg_ana
  FROM Examination
  WHERE ANA IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ana) as mean_value
  FROM per_id_avg
)
SELECT 
  p.ID,
  p.avg_ana,
  p.avg_ana - o.mean_value as gap
FROM per_id_avg p
CROSS JOIN overall_mean o
WHERE p.avg_ana > o.mean_value
ORDER BY gap DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "how far above the mean" means absolute difference (avg_ana - overall_mean), not percentage or ratio

alternatives.interpretation: "how far above the mean" could mean percentage increase above the overall mean (e.g., 25% higher)
alternatives.sql:
WITH per_id_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(ANA) as avg_ana
  FROM Examination
  WHERE ANA IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ana) as mean_value
  FROM per_id_avg
)
SELECT 
  p.ID,
  p.avg_ana,
  ROUND(((p.avg_ana - o.mean_value) / o.mean_value) * 100, 2) as pct_above_mean
FROM per_id_avg p
CROSS JOIN overall_mean o
WHERE p.avg_ana > o.mean_value
ORDER BY pct_above_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;
